task.title: Record an edit under a name other than the checkout's Git email
task.description:
Every edit Workbook records carries the name of whoever made it, and that name is always the Git `user.email` of the checkout the command ran in. Workbook reads it once per process and offers no way to say otherwise. Anyone building a hosted tool on the CLI has one checkout acting for many signed-in people, so every edit would carry the server's name.

This story lets a caller name the person an edit is recorded under, through an environment variable. It is meant for hosting. "Run the board behind a sign-in proxy" builds the web side on top of it.

## How it behaves

- With the variable set, the command records its edits under that name instead of the checkout's `user.email`. With it unset, nothing changes.
- The given name is the person for everything Workbook decides by identity: `--assign self` assigns to it, `workbook next` skips tasks held by anybody else, and only that name or the recorder may remove its assignment.
- A folder with no `user.email` configured works when the variable is set. A tasks-only server folder has no natural Git identity of its own.
- The name is asserted, exactly like `user.email` is today. Workbook does not verify it and keeps no list of who is allowed. The statement in `docs/architecture.md` that there is no roster stays true.

## Out of scope

- A label that tells a person's own agent apart from that person on their own machine. Decided against: locally, the checkout's name is enough.
- Checking that the name belongs to anyone. Whoever can set the variable can already push.

## Decisions to settle before building

Settle these first and record the outcome on this task; each one that turns into real work becomes its own task depending on this one.

1. The variable's name, and whether a command-line flag is offered as well.
2. What a name may be. Proposed: whatever an assignment already accepts as a person, since `self` has to resolve to it.
3. What the Git commit behind an edit says about author and committer when the name is overridden. The operation is the record; the commit is attribution only.

## Done when

- With the variable set, `create`, `update`, a comment, an attachment and an assignment are each recorded under the given name, and `workbook show --history` shows it.
- `--assign self`, `workbook next` and removing an assignment all treat the given name as the person.
- The same commands work in a folder with no `user.email` when the variable is set.
- An empty or unusable value is refused with a validation error. It never falls back to the checkout's name without saying so.
- With the variable unset, every command writes exactly what it writes today.
- `docs/reference.md` documents the variable, and `docs/architecture.md` says an asserted name can come from it.
